mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a three-month window indicates a paradoxical labor market signal (e.g., underemployment or part-time necessity), which precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises while UNRATE rises over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise over any 3-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 500k units for three consecutive months, coupled with a rising CPIAUCSL above 2.5% in the same period, signals a housing demand shock and inflationary pressure, which jointly predict negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when HOUST < 500k for 3 months and CPIAUCSL > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than one year in a low-inflation environment signals an extended accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for > 12 months AND CPIAUCSL inflation < 2%
regime_hint: prolonged monetary accommodation with low inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when FEDFUNDS < 1% for over a year and inflation remains below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive quarters, accompanied by a falling unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals improving demand and labor conditions, which jointly predict positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month MA for 3 consecutive quarters AND UNRATE falls
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when GDPC1 is above its 12-month MA for three quarters and UNRATE is falling.
